segments.text: Z-test, t-test, chi-square, ANOVA. Which one should you use?
segments.caption: z-test, t-test, chi-square, ANOVA. Which one should you use?

segments.text: Pick the wrong test, and your answer is wrong. This one video tells you exactly which test to use. Save it!
segments.caption: Pick the wrong test, and your answer is wrong. This one video tells you exactly which test to use. Save it!

segments.text: Choosing a test comes down to two questions.
segments.caption: Choosing a test comes down to two questions.

segments.text: One: what kind of data? Numbers you can average, like weight or time? Or categories you count, like tea or coffee?
segments.caption: One: what kind of data? Numbers you can average, like weight or time? Or categories you count, like tea or coffee?

segments.text: Two: how many groups are you comparing?
segments.caption: Two: how many groups are you comparing?

segments.text: Z-test.
segments.caption: z-test.

segments.text: Compare one average with a claim, when sigma, the population's spread, is known, or the sample is large.
segments.caption: Compare one average with a claim, when sigma, the population's spread, is known, or the sample is large.

segments.text: Do these juice bottles really hold two hundred milliliters? We checked a hundred of them.
segments.caption: Do these juice bottles really hold 200 ml? We checked 100 of them.

segments.text: Or: are a city's five hundred students scoring above the national average?
segments.caption: Or: are a city's 500 students scoring above the national average?

segments.text: One-sample t-test.
segments.caption: One-sample t-test.

segments.text: Same question, but the sample is small and sigma is unknown. That's most of real life.
segments.caption: Same question, but the sample is small and sigma is unknown. That's most of real life.

segments.text: Do these ten phones really last twenty hours, like the ad says?
segments.caption: Do these 10 phones really last 20 hours, like the ad says?

segments.text: Or: is a café's average wait really five minutes? We timed twelve orders.
segments.caption: Or: is a café's average wait really 5 minutes? We timed 12 orders.

segments.text: Two-sample t-test.
segments.caption: Two-sample t-test.

segments.text: Two separate groups. Are their averages different?
segments.caption: Two separate groups. Are their averages different?

segments.text: Battery life of brand A, versus brand B.
segments.caption: Battery life of brand A, versus brand B.

segments.text: Or: do online students score differently from classroom students?
segments.caption: Or: do online students score differently from classroom students?

segments.text: Paired t-test.
segments.caption: Paired t-test.

segments.text: The same people, measured twice: before and after.
segments.caption: The same people, measured twice: before and after.

segments.text: Typing speed before a course, and after it.
segments.caption: Typing speed before a course, and after it.

segments.text: Or: the same runners, timed in old shoes, and then in new shoes.
segments.caption: Or: the same runners, timed in old shoes, and then in new shoes.

segments.text: ANOVA.
segments.caption: ANOVA.

segments.text: Three or more groups. Is any of their averages different?
segments.caption: Three or more groups. Is any of their averages different?

segments.text: Waiting times at three coffee shops.
segments.caption: Waiting times at three coffee shops.

segments.text: Or: which of four ad designs brings the most sales?
segments.caption: Or: which of 4 ad designs brings the most sales?

segments.text: Chi-square test of independence.
segments.caption: Chi-square test of independence.

segments.text: Now the data are categories. Are two of them linked?
segments.caption: Now the data are categories. Are two of them linked?

segments.text: Does preferring tea or coffee depend on age?
segments.caption: Does preferring tea or coffee depend on age?

segments.text: Or: is the phone brand people buy linked to the city they live in?
segments.caption: Or: is the phone brand people buy linked to the city they live in?

segments.text: Chi-square goodness of fit.
segments.caption: Chi-square goodness of fit.

segments.text: One category. Do the counts match what you expected?
segments.caption: One category. Do the counts match what you expected?

segments.text: Is this dice fair? Roll it sixty times, and count each face.
segments.caption: Is this dice fair? Roll it 60 times, and count each face.

segments.text: Or: do customers really visit evenly across all seven days of the week?
segments.caption: Or: do customers really visit evenly across all 7 days of the week?

segments.text: Bonus interview tip: t-tests and ANOVA assume the data are roughly normal.
segments.caption: Bonus interview tip: t-tests and ANOVA assume the data are roughly normal.

segments.text: Small sample, heavily skewed? Swap them: Mann-Whitney for the two-sample t-test, Wilcoxon for paired, and Kruskal-Wallis for ANOVA.
segments.caption: Small sample, heavily skewed? Swap them: Mann-Whitney for the two-sample t-test, Wilcoxon for paired, and Kruskal-Wallis for ANOVA.

segments.text: Here's the full cheat sheet.
segments.caption: Here's the full cheat sheet.

segments.text: Averages? One group: z or t. Two groups: two-sample or paired t. Three or more: ANOVA. Counts? Chi-square.
segments.caption: Averages? One group: z or t. Two groups: two-sample or paired t. Three or more: ANOVA. Counts? Chi-square.
